text.p: Italian bond futures held to higher levels in late afternoon trade after shrugging off a report of a plan for Italy to delay its EMU entry beyond 1999 while taking some support from the stronger lira, dealers said.
A report in the Financial Times newspaper said that Italy would be offered a deal to delay its EMU entry until 2000 or 2001, but the idea was quickly denied by officials in Rome, Brussels and Bonn.
Bond futures immediately fell on the report then rallied as the denials underpined investors belief Italy was still determined to take the tough medicine to meet the 1999 deadline.
"The market is trusting Prodi on this one, and hoping that he will stick to the tough measures needed to get Italy's finances back to health," said one LIFFE trader.

Many investors had already believed it would be difficult for Italy to meet the Maastricht criteria for EMU entry in 1999 and that any compromise may be beneficial for Italy if it gave a definate date for Italy's entry into EMU.
German doubts over Italy making the first wave of EMU entrants had pushed bonds down earlier this week, but many analysts see other European nations finding difficulties in meeting the EMU criteria.

Dealers pointed out that the performance of BTPs was particularly encouraging considering the early weakness of U.S. T-bonds, but the mood was generally uncertain and many investors were waiting to take profits on any rally.
